name: three-color-inputs-color-attachment

This case observes attachment 0: the float4 color (color + tint) / 2, which reads the half tint. Every lane is exact (dyadic floats, normal halves, wrapping integers), so the three cases pin the input-attachment index of each class and the ordering across attachments.

name: convolution-gradient-reduction-four-splits-ten-channels
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-output-channels case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero thread count stops every thread at the entry's bound. Function constant 123 = 0: weightsFormat 0, no linking (the sum is stored straight to destination, binding 27), no 2D blocking. tThreads = oThreads = 3, magicOThreads = (3, 0x55555556, 2) (n / 3 for every n below 2^16), outputChannels = 10 (oMod4 = 2), destinationChannels = 12, numSplits = 4, numWeightsRoundedUp4 = 12. A threadgroup of 4 threads: thread 3 fails tid < tThreads; threads 0 and 1 (channels 0-3, 4-7, both below outputChannels) load a float4 from each of the 4 splits (stride 12 floats) and store the float4 sum; thread 2 (channels 8 and 9) takes the oMod4 = 2 branch, loading and storing two floats. The source's split s, channel c holds ((7c + 3s + cs) mod 11) - 5 (nonlinear, so a wrong split or channel changes the answer) and 999 in the two padding channels, which nothing reads. Every value is an integer of magnitude at most 5 and every sum of 4 at most 20: exact in float in any order. Destination words 0 to 9 are the sums, each written by one thread, and words 10 and 11 keep the 0xab fill. Every loop is finite by these inputs: the split loops run numSplits - 1 = 3 times.

name: gradient-samples-and-comparisons-of-3d-cube-and-depth-textures
rationale: The sampling forms D283 decodes (family B), in a kernel: lane i reads Lane i of buffer 0 (six float4s: the 3D/2D coordinate and comparison reference; dP/dx and the array layer; dP/dy; the cube direction; the cube dP/dx; the cube dP/dy) and writes six float4s to out[6i .. 6i + 5] of buffer 1, pre-filled with 0xAB: a gradient sample of texture 0 (3D rgba16_float 4x4x4), of texture 1 (cube rgba16_float 4x4), and of texture 2 (cube array, 2 cubes), through a constexpr sampler whose minification is linear and magnification nearest, so the gradients choose the filter: even lanes have zero gradients (nearest), odd lanes gradients of half the coordinate range along x (and y), LOD 1 (linear); the coordinate lies a quarter texel right of a texel centre, so the linear result is 0.75 and 0.25 of two texels of small integers, exact; the cube direction names a face texel the same way on each of the six faces (|major axis| 1, never at a face edge), its gradient a unit step of the face's s. Then the gradient samples (nearest) of textures 3-6 (depth32_float 2D 4x4, 2D array 4x4x2, cube 4x4, cube array 2 cubes; distinct depths in (0, 1)), their gradient comparisons (less_equal, the reference the 2D texel itself on every third lane, else half or 1.5 times it), and the depth cube array's sample at level 0 and by default (level 0 in a kernel) and the depth cube and cube array comparisons at level 0. 64 lanes. The AIR has no loop.

name: a14-nhwc-float-2x2-kernel-six-by-five-channels-two-images
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's zero-extent case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC). Constant 89 = 0x56 states C mod 16 = 6 and O mod 16 = 5 and selects no linking, no reduction, not 1x1 and not the 16x16 multiply (bit 17 clear); constant 124 = 0x101b607 selects unit stride, unit dilation, one group, NHWC (bit 26 clear), tiles O = C = K = 8, one k-split and one simdgroup per threadgroup, both tiles in registers (no threadgroup staging), the image edge check, and C and O not multiples of their tiles. So the entry takes the A14 NHWC kernel, which multiplies float 8x8 simdgroup matrices into float accumulators, each lane building its two fragment cells from its lane index (the device-measured layout: row ((L >> 1) & 3) | ((L >> 4) << 2), columns ((L >> 3) & 1) 4 + (L & 1) 2 and the next). The 448-byte parameters (binding 26): 6 input and 5 output channels, a 2 x 2 kernel, batch 2 in one sub-batch, a 5 x 2 source and a 5 x 2 gradient, offsets (-1, 0), 10 gradient positions per image (one full 8-position chunk and a 2-position tail), 16-bit magic divisors 2 (kW, kH) and 5 (gradient width) and the 32-bit divisor 5, uber tiles 1, per-image element counts 50 and 60, weightsOutputChannels 5, numWeights 120. Four threadgroups of 32 threads, threadgroup x = ky 2 + kx, each compute dW[ky][kx][c][o] = sum over n, gy, gx of gradient[n][gy][gx][o] source[n][gy + ky][gx + kx - 1][c], loading zero for positions left of the source, channels past 6 and output channels past 5, and store it to destination word ((ky 2 + kx) 6 + c) 5 + o (HWIO; binding 27, poisoned 0xab, all 120 words written). Every source and gradient value is one of [-3.5, -3.0, -2.5, -2.0, -1.5, -1.0, -0.5, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 5.0], exact in float (exponents where both 8-bit conventions agree): source element i takes entry (7i + 3) mod 16, gradient element i entry (3i + 5) mod 16. Every product is a multiple of 1/4 of magnitude at most 25 and every sum (at most 20 terms) lies in [-35.75, 51.0], so every word is exact in any summation order; no output is zero. Loops are bounded by the two images, the two chunks per image and the fixed tile counts.

name: square-root-a-gathered-two-by-two-block-in-place
rationale:
A half-precision tone map that gathers a 2x2 block, transforms each of the four texels and writes them back to the same four positions. It covers air.sqrt.v4f16, which no case reached before; 20 corpus sources carry it.
The gather is what makes the case worth more than its arithmetic. The embedded constexpr sampler is coord::pixel, nearest, clamp_to_edge, so the translator emulates it with a level-zero fetch rather than a Vulkan gather, and the shader then routes lane 3 to (2gx, 2gy), lane 2 to (2gx+1, 2gy), lane 1 to (2gx+1, 2gy+1) and lane 0 to (2gx, 2gy+1). Under Metal's gather order that composition is the identity per texel, so the derivation is out[j][i] = f(in[j][i]) and does not have to encode the convention -- but every 2x2 block here carries four different values, so a lane order that disagrees with Metal's writes them to the wrong texels and the case fails. The derivation is convention-independent and the test is not.
Every value is exact in half by construction. The input is 1 - n^2/128 for n = (i + 3j) mod 9, a multiple of 1/128 in [0.5, 1]; subtracting 0.5, doubling, clamping at zero and subtracting from one all stay on the 1/64 grid; the scale is 16, a power of two, so the argument to the square root is exactly n^2/4 and the root is exactly n/2. Feeding air.sqrt.v4f16 nothing but perfect squares is deliberate: it is what makes the answer independent of whether the square root is reached through Metal's precise or fast variant.
Nine distinct values across 64 texels, and the whole shader is a per-texel map, so a dropped write, a swapped lane or a mis-scaled clamp all change bytes.

name: five-elements-of-eight-threads
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-destination case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero destination extent returns at the bounds check. The user constant maps the four destination dimensions to themselves (xMap 0, yMap 1, zMap 2, wMap 3), so every lane of the destination coordinate is defined. Eight threads of one threadgroup each take element x = thread; the destination extent is 5 (dstSize 5, 1, 1, 1), so threads 5 to 7 return and threads 0 to 4 read one 4-bit index (fallback offset 2, stride 1: nibble 2 + x) and write destination element x. Every retained prefixSecondary_f module, the LUT read, returns +0.0, so elements 0 to 4 hold +0.0 and 5 to 7 keep the 0xab fill: the 8 observed words show the destination bound and coordinates. Each element is written by one thread; the kernel has no loop.

name: linked-gather-vector-matrix-half-k439-second-matrix-tg-reduction
rationale: Reaching variant of 755b3092 (linked-zero-k-gather-vector-matrix-half), whose zero kernel-info word and params leave the kernel no K and no rows (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC). The constants select an Apple device (constant 127 bit 10) whose threadgroup shape comes from the kernel-info word: 8 simdgroups, 32 threads along K and 8 rows (grid and threadgroup 32x8x1); the gather (constant 124 bit 13, every threadgroup id kept), 4-wide B loads, a K tile of 2, the partial reduction step, the K tail (not divisible by 4), the alpha multiply, the y edge check, the threadgroup-memory reduction (no simd reduction: 1024 bytes, one float per thread) and the linked destination callback. N = 8 rows of K = 439: the two whole steps (numDeviceReductionsDownTileK 2) cover elements 0 to 255, the partial steps 2 and 3 (numDeviceReductions 4) elements 256 to 435 (K4 = 436: lanes 0 to 12 of step 3), and thread 0 of each row the tail 436 to 438. P = 1 and indices[0] = 1, so the kernel reads the second of two half A matrices (AMatrixBytes = 8 rows of 440 elements): A_e[n][k] = (5k + 3n + floor(kn/4) + 2e) mod 7 - 3, so expert 0 would give other sums; B[k] = (3k + floor(k/5)) mod 5 - 1 (half, BRowBytes one element). Thread (0, n) writes alpha * D[n] (alpha 0.5) through the callback at coordinate n: table entry 1's 8 floats, each written once. Every product is an integer of magnitude at most 9 and every partial sum an integer below 2^12, exact in float in any order, and the alpha product is exact. Every loop is finite by these inputs: the step counts, K4 and the constant thread counts bound the reduction loops, and the tree halves 32 to 1.

name: linked-zero-k-gather-vector-matrix-half

name: primitive-acceleration-structure-intersection
rationale: A downward ray hits one authored counter-clockwise triangle at unit distance; all observable triangle-intersection result fields are compared exactly.

name: the-same-triangle-wound-the-other-way-faces-the-other-way
rationale: The companion of the counter-clockwise primitive-intersection case: the same three vertices in the opposite order, hit by the same ray. Everything the kernel reports is unchanged except triangle_front_facing and the barycentric pair, so the case pins the winding-to-facing contract that a cull mode is defined against.

name: float-to-half-rounding-at-the-half-range-edge-and-denormals
rationale: Thread i reads the float vectors (x, y, z) from in[3i .. 3i + 2] and writes 16 words, each 4-lane half result as two words (lane 0 in the low half of the first): half(x), half(y), hx + hy, hx * hy, hx - hy, fma(hx, hy, hz), half(x * y) and hx * hy + hz, where hx, hy and hz are half(x), half(y) and half(z). x runs over the edge of the half range of both signs (65504 and its float neighbours, 65512 and its neighbours, the largest float below 65520, 65520 and above, 65536, 1e5, infinity), ties of the half normal grid (2049, 2051, 4097, 1 + 2^-11) and the half denormals and their ties (2^-25, 3 * 2^-26, 2^-24, 2^-15, below 2^-14); y and z bring sums, differences and products of halves onto the same edges. It measures how Metal rounds a float to half there: to nearest even, every value from 65504 up to below 65520 to 65504 and from 65520 up to infinity (docs/TODO.md 2.1). Compiled without fast math.

name: linked-single-invocation-zero-bin
rationale: One invocation is bounded by source_size 1x1. Linking is enabled with one authored texture and one address-table element; the exact callback is loop-free and returns float4 zero without dereferencing either resource. The one-bin histogram parameters force every active scalar lane to bin zero, and the poisoned counter makes the bounded global-atomic write observable byte-exactly.

name: vertex-device-and-constant-pointer-integer-differences
rationale: One vertex invocation computes 12- and 28-byte interior-pointer differences through 64- and 32-bit integer conversions. No derived address is dereferenced. Input allocations are 32 and 48 bytes; stores cover bytes 8..40 of a 48-byte output and preserve both eight-byte canaries. Expected words: [0xcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcd,12,28,12,28,0xcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcd]. The vertex case disables rasterization; the fragment case uses a 1x1 attachmentless pass. Both source bodies are loop-free.

name: write-short4-through-a-short-coordinate-into-one-plane
rationale: The signed plane of the same fixture, pinning air.write_texture_2d.i16.s.v4i16. The corpus already has a signed short texture write (write-four-shorts-no-signed-byte-could-hold) but only at a uint2 coordinate and only at a single texel; this one writes sixteen distinct texels through a ushort2 coordinate, with lanes -32768+i, -129-x, 128+y and 32767-i, so the extreme shorts and the coordinate arithmetic are checked together.

name: write-uint4-through-a-short-coordinate-into-three-array-slices
rationale: The uint4 half of a kernel whose three writes are the corpus's first authored short-coordinate texture writes. The coordinate is a ushort2 and the array slice a ushort, so the AIR call is air.write_texture_2d_array.i16.u.v4i32 rather than the uint2 spelling the corpus already covers -- a 16-bit coordinate word, which a lowering that sign-extends it or truncates the slice would resolve to a different texel. Sixteen threads each write all three slices, and every texel's four lanes are derived from its own x, y and slice, so a swapped coordinate pair, a dropped slice or a permuted lane order is a content mismatch instead of a silently identical image. Two lanes exceed sixteen bits (0xDEADBEEF^idx and 0x80000000+idx), so a storage image one step narrower cannot carry them.

name: write-ushort4-through-a-short-coordinate-into-three-array-slices
rationale: The ushort4 half of the same fixture, pinning air.write_texture_2d_array.i16.u.v4i16: an unsigned 16-bit value written to a 2D array through a ushort2 coordinate and a ushort slice. The four lanes are 0xFFFF-idx, 0x8000+idx, 256+x and 300+y over sixteen threads and three slices -- every lane above the unsigned byte range, and every texel distinct, so neither an eight-bit storage image nor a mixed-up coordinate can reproduce the image.

name: imageblock-extent-queries-and-a-neighbours-cell
rationale: One 4x2 threadgroup with an explicit imageblock of 4x2 Cell {float value; ushort2 at;} cells, the size of the threadgroup. Every thread stages value = x + 100 y and at = (x, y) in its own cell, and after the imageblock barrier reads the cell of its right-hand neighbour, wrapping at the width the imageblock's get_width() answers, and reports get_width() and get_height() (access.imageblock.extent, DESIGN D173, D213): out[y * 4 + x] = (bits(float((x + 1) % 4) + 100 y), ((x + 1) % 4) | (y << 16), 4, 2). Each cell names its own coordinates, so a wrong extent or cell stride reads a value that names another cell. The AIR has no loop.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-four-2x2-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2, 3, and 4 and receives exact float4 zero from all three linked _uber_clear bodies. A six-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x2 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x2 resource.

name: linked-single-unit-complex-pad-gradient
rationale: A 1x1 grid, unit widths, unit source and destination extents, unit divisors, and zero padding bound every dimension loop to one iteration. The exact complex secondary prefix returns (0,0) and the overwrite specialization selects the exact complex primary postfix, which writes both zero components to the sole poisoned destination element.

name: two-16-texture-arrays-share-one-constexpr-sampler
rationale: DESIGN D299: a fullscreen draw into a 16x16 rgba32_float target. Pixel (x, y) adds the sample of element x of the 16-texture array a at [[texture(0)]] and of element y of the 16-texture array b at [[texture(16)]], each at (0.5, 0.5), implicit LOD, through one constexpr nearest, clamp-to-edge, normalized sampler (two sampler.sample_hoisted_grad.switch). Each element is a 1x1 rgba32_float texture of one level, so each sample is its one texel: a[i] = (i, 0, 1, 0.5) and b[j] = (0, j, 2, 0.25). So target(x, y) = (x, y, 3, 0.75), exact; a swapped or misnumbered element shows in the first two channels. Where the profile has fewer than 32 samplers per stage both arrays sample through the stage's one separate sampler; this case is that form's observation. The observation is the whole target, initially 0xab. The AIR has no loop.
